text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Thursday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Chairman of parliament Vytautas Landsbregis said that it did not make much of a difference whether Lithuania got into NATO now or later. He made the comments after meeting the NATO deputy secretary general in Brussels on Wednesday.
- The members of parliament's national security comittee went to examine the situation with border controls on the Lithuanian-Belarus border.
- The tax inspection says that the budget failed to collect 41 million litas in January.
- Two Russian citizens were detained at a border check point on Tuesday on the suspicion they may be hired hitman.
- Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas vetoed the law on new procedures to appoint the prosecutor general passed by parliament in February.
- The government wants to compensate the population for lost savings due to hyper-inflation in 1991 from the privatisation fund.
- The state border control system needs rapid reform, said parliament's national security comittee after a recent visit to the Lithuania-Belarus border.
- The construction costs of Butinge oil terminal are some $260 million. Aproximately the same amount of money to liquidate the problem-struck Innovation bank.
